evidence: η written ει; sense “maimed” = ἀναπήρους (Luke 14:13,21). Nestle 1904 ἀναπήρους; LSJ ἀναπήρος. Not Berean apparatus choice.
Mark 16:18. The bracketed clause wrote unaccented και for καὶ.
John 8:4. αυτοφώρῳ has no breathing. The other αὐτός forms in this text use upsilon with psili (U+1F50).
Postpositive δὲ is not capitalized. The article is already written in Mark 6:50, Luke 8:30, Luke 9:59, Luke 24:19, Acts 9:1, and Acts 22:28. Nestle 1904 writes δὲ.
Luke 13:4. The number eight takes a smooth breathing; the grave stays because another word follows. Nestle 1904 ὀκτὼ. The compound note keeps the undertie.
Luke 13:11. δέκα ὀκτώ stands before a comma, so the acute stays. Nestle 1904 ὀκτώ. The compound note keeps the undertie.
Revelation 17:5. μεγάλη is feminine, so the uncial article is Η. The same line already writes Η in ΜΗΤΗΡ. Nestle 1904 reads Η ΜΕΓΑΛΗ.
Revelation 17:5. μήτηρ is feminine, so the uncial article is Η. Nestle 1904 reads Η ΜΗΤΗΡ.
1 Peter 1:13. τελείως modifies ἐλπίσατε. Nestle 1904 has no comma between them.
John 4:35. ἤδη opens the next sentence, which verse 36 continues. Nestle 1904 places the period before ἤδη.
John 4:36. The sentence began at ἤδη, so the article is not a capital. Nestle 1904 reads ὁ θερίζων.
1 Corinthians 10:19. The two ὅτι clauses are parallel questions. This edition writes the question mark as ;. Nestle 1904 has the same break.
1 Corinthians 12:3. The cry is uncial, and ΙΗΣΟΥΣ is already in capitals. Nestle 1904 reads ΑΝΑΘΕΜΑ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ.
1 Corinthians 12:3. The same cry. Κυριος had neither an accent nor the capitals of ΙΗΣΟΥΣ. Nestle 1904 reads ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ.
